name.text: 26.3 Circle Theorems - Angle to Centre, Intersecting Chords

questiontext.text:
Points \(A,B,C,D\) lie on the circle centred at \(O\).
The point \(E\) is the intersection of the lines \(AB\) and \(CD\).
Diagram not to scale.

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

Using the properties of intersecting chords: \(AE \times BE = CE \times DE\)

\(CE = \frac{AE \times BE}{DE}\)

\(CE = \frac{{@segAE@} \times {@segAE+segAB@}}{{@segDE@}}\)

\(CD + {@segDE@} = {@tans1+segDE@}\)

Therefore \(CD = {@tans1@}cm\)

You have correctly found the length \(CE\).
However, you have forgotten to subtract the length of \(DE\) to find \(CD\).

You have used the formula \(AB \times AE = CD \times DE\).
However, the correct relationship between the chords is \(AE \times BE = CE \times DE\).

Remember that you should use the distance from each point on the circle to the intersection point.

You have incorrectly related the chords using the formula: {@if abs(ans1-((segDE*(segAE+segAB)/segAE)-segDE))<=0.1 then "\\(BE \\times DE = AE \\times CE\\)" else if abs(ans1-((segAE*segDE/(segAE+segAB))-segDE))<=0.1 then "\\(AE \\times DE = BE \\times CE\\)"@}
The correct relationship between the chords is: \(AE \times BE = CE \times DE\)

Remember that the product of the lengths of the chords which lie on the same line are equal.

You have incorrectly related the chords using the formula: {@if abs(ans1-(segDE*segAB/segAE))<=0.1 then "\\(AB \\times DE = AE \\times CD\\)" else if abs(ans1-(segAE*segDE/segAB))<=0.1 then "\\(AE \\times DE = AB \\times CD\\)"@}
The correct relationship between the chords is: \(AE \times BE = CE \times DE\)

Remember that you should use the distance from each point on the circle to the intersection point and that the product of the lengths of the chords which lie on the same line are equal.

Here is a worked solution:

Using the circle theorem: "An angle subtended at the circumference by a diameter is a right angle", the angle \(BCD = 90^\circ\).

So, using trigonometry, \(\cos(CDB) = \frac{CD}{BD}\)

Using part (a):

\(\cos(CDB) = \frac{{@tans1@}}{{@2*rad@}}\)

\(CDB = {@acos(tans1/(2*rad))@}\)

\(CDB = {@decimalplaces(acos(tans1/(2*rad))*180/%pi,5)@}...^\circ\)


Using the circle theorem: "An angle formed at the centre of a sector is twice the angle formed at the circumference": the angle \(COB\) is twice the angle \(CDB\).

\(COB = {@decimalplaces(acos(tans1/(2*rad))*360/%pi,5)@}...^\circ\)
